# 我们怎样理解两个人之间的关系\n\n版本：v0.1｜2026-09-07｜观: # How Do We Understand the Relationship Between Two People? Version: v0.1 | 2026-09-07 | Candidate perspective and method draft **Our starting point: character tendencies supply the raw material; the ways two people respond to each other constitute their relationship; situations and choices drive that relationship to change.** One pairing name can hold many stories. Its greatest value is showing what problems these two people may encounter again and again when placed together. This article presents this project's own framework. It draws on general relationship research in [Psychological Foundations](01_%E5%BF%83%E7%90%86%E5%AD%A6%E5%BA%95%E5%B1%82.md). The arrangement of the six specific mechanisms, the four-axis comparison, the naming system, and the approach to writing storylines were developed by this project and have not been validated as a relationship-prediction model. ## 1. What Each of the Three Layers Answers | Layer | The reader's question | Responsibility | Status | |---|---|---|---| | Psychological foundations | What mechanisms in human interaction are worth understanding? | Explain the research questions, findings, methods, and scope | An accessible synthesis of existing research | | Our middle-layer perspective | How can we use this knowledge to analyze these 16 characters? | Define our choices, observation steps, and creative method | A method proposed by this project | | Pair-relationship layer | What is this pair called, and what can we discuss, write, or draw about them? | Provide a pairing name, two-way perspectives, scenes, and turning points | Character-based situational storytelling | Readers can enter at any layer. Starting from a pairing name and moving downward reveals the relationship mechanisms it uses; going farther shows what the relevant research actually supports. Starting from the research and moving upward also shows where our own interpretation and creative work enter the process. ## 2. Four Questions, Asked of Each Person Separately First expand A's and B's four axes. Each axis describes only a relative priority in relevant situations; it does not lock a person into the same response forever. | Four-axis question | What to establish for A and B separately | What to ask when they are together | |---|---|---| | **What do they contend for: Gain / Control** | Do they prioritize securing material returns, or decision-making authority and confirmation of status? | Can both get what they need? Are they competing for the same thing? Who has the right to allocate it? | | **How do they push: Strategy / Pressure** | Are they more likely to rearrange information, relationships, and options, or directly raise the cost of refusal? | Can the two approaches work in sequence? Do they undermine each other? Who bears the cost of acting openly? | | **When do they stop: Instrumental / Punitive** | Once the external goal has been achieved, is there still value in making the other person pay? | Does one person think the matter is over while the other believes a debt remains? | | **How do they present it: Justification / Disregard** | Do their actions or later explanations rely more on respectable, norm-based justification, or less on that kind of approval? | Who needs an explanation for outsiders? Who might support, exploit, or puncture that explanation? | For example, Broker and Puppet Master are both Strategy, Instrumental, and Justification; their difference lies in Gain versus Control. This lets us pose a relationship question: if returns and decision-making authority can be satisfied separately, how do they trade? If Puppet Master changes the allocation to secure authority, how does Broker respond? That is a starting point for writing; the specific task and each side's leverage still need to be established. **Definition check.** This draft follows *Core Model and Product Definitions v1.0*. Strategy may involve designing a situation openly, and Pressure may be applied through precise procedures. Some passages in the existing *Theoretical Foundations and Model Notes v0.1* frame Strategy as more covert; this draft does not adopt that narrower definition. Props and actions in the character assets may supply imagery, but concealed identities within those assets are not presented as real-world occupations or personality diagnoses. ## 3. Six Relationship Mechanisms These mechanisms may occur simultaneously. Each relationship card selects the two or three that best explain its scene, helping readers explore further; the number of tags does not indicate relationship intensity. ### M01 Collusion and the Contest for Position: What Does Each Person Want to Preserve in the Same Game? **Our perspective.** To understand whether two characters can work side by side, first examine how their shared outcome is produced and who allocates it. The same goal may put people on the same path or make them compete for a single position; different goals may sometimes enable exchange. We place “whether both goals can be satisfied” and “who controls the conditions for achieving them” ahead of character similarity. Four things deserve attention: whether a shared task truly exists; whether gains and decision-making authority can be separated; what each side controls; and how many alternatives either side has without the other. Actual power in a relationship arises from these conditions and cannot be read directly from the label “Control type.” **Original scenario.** Broker provides access while Puppet Master coordinates the parties. They may need each other while the agreed gains and scope of authority are both respected. If that access becomes replaceable, the original allocation may be challenged. The reversal comes from a change in leverage; no one needs to switch type abruptly. **Writing prompts:** “What can we accomplish together?” “Once it is done, who still needs to remain?” Research pathways: interdependence theory and power-dependence analysis. [S01](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.psych.54.101601.145059), [S02](https://doi.org/10.2307/2089716). The research supports analyzing interaction through situations and dependencies; the character storyline above is original to this draft. ### M02 Mirroring and Complementarity: Recognizing Your Move—and Perhaps Following It **Our perspective.** Similar behavioral languages readily create a sense of “you understand me,” but they can also lead two people to compete for the same position. Different methods may support a division of labor or produce a dispute over approach. We retain all four possibilities—shared language, shared blind spots, differences that enable coordination, and differences that cause friction—without assigning an overall positive or negative verdict to similarity or opposition. Keep three things separate: how similar the two actually are; how similar they perceive each other to be; and whether their current behavior can work together. Dominance and affiliation in interpersonal complementarity research are also not equivalent to Control and Justification in our four axes. **Original scenario.** Two Brokers both understand the unstated reservations in a deal, so negotiations can be economical. If each wants the other to reveal their true share first, that shared language turns into mutual wariness. Puppet Master and Enforcer may divide the work between arranging the route and driving execution, yet still dispute who is entitled to change the plan. **Writing prompt:** “Can you do the part I cannot, or are you taking my place?” Research pathways: goal and behavioral complementarity, interaction rhythms, and actual versus perceived similarity. [S03](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.72.3.592), [S04](https://doi.org/10.1037/a0016232), [S05](https://doi.org/10.1177/0146167214557002), [S06](https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407508096700). These studies also suggest that coordination in interaction, subjective satisfaction, and long-term relationship quality should be discussed separately. ### M03 Mismatched Ledgers: The Same Contribution Is Entered in Different Books **Our perspective.** Many conflicts arise because the parties have not agreed on how the relationship should be accounted for. One treats help as an exchange, while the other sees it as care among one's own people; one talks about equal shares, while the other talks about seniority; one thinks payment settled the matter, while the other is still waiting for acknowledgment. We examine the current rules through four plain questions: Is help given according to need? Is priority ranked by status? Is turn-taking or equal repayment expected? Are contributions and returns calculated proportionally? These questions draw on relational models theory, but real relationships may use different rules for different matters. Gain types cannot be reduced to exchange alone, and Control types cannot be treated as always demanding obedience. **Original scenario.** Broker believes the agreed compensation has made good the loss. Smiler believes it repaid only the material account and did not address the slight. The same compensation may count as closure to one person and a brush-off to the other. **Writing prompt:** “What do you think you have already repaid? What does the other person think you still owe?” Research pathways: exchange and communal relationships; relational models theory. [S07](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.37.1.12), [S08](https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-295X.99.4.689). “Mismatched ledgers” is our accessible organizing term, not a separate psychological scale. ### M04 Escalation and Ceasefire: How One Response Pushes the Next Round Further **Our perspective.** Roles within a relationship change with the issue. First identify who is asking for change this time and who wants to preserve the status quo; then write the questioning, escalation, silence, delay, or counterattack. A Strategist may pursue intensely, and a Pressure type may refuse to respond. Do not map these two modes directly onto anxious or avoidant attachment. Each cycle should specify at least three steps: what triggered it; how A interpreted and answered; and how B understood that answer. When writing a turn, add an observable stopping action, such as pausing further conditions, responding to one clear request, or returning the power to choose. A ceasefire, accepting consequences, and rebuilding trust may be separate stages. **Original scenario.** A Arbiter presses for an answer about who will bear the loss, while the other person delays verification. The former reads delay as refusal to acknowledge the debt and adds demands; the latter reads escalation as proof that agreement is impossible and withdraws further. If they first separate confirmed items from disputed ones, the story may find an opening for a ceasefire. Simply falling silent cannot automatically be written as resolution. **Writing prompt:** “If one person stops responding in the same way as the previous round, where does the story change?” Research pathways: demand-withdraw patterns, related meta-analysis, and accommodation research. [S09](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.59.1.73), [S10](https://doi.org/10.1080/03637751.2013.813632), [S11](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.60.1.53). This draft's “ceasefire conditions” are narrative and observational questions; they do not guarantee that any real relationship will be repaired. ### M05 Frontstage and Backstage: The Audience Changes What the Same Words Do **Our perspective.** An unseen third party may stand between two people: colleagues, friends, an organization, onlookers, or rules both recognize. Justification / Disregard describes different degrees of reliance on such approval; audiences, evidence, and the consequences of action also change how the two express themselves. We ask: Who needs a defensible account? Who vouches for whom? Who will contradict the other in public? Can their private understanding withstand the consequences of becoming public? A shared line can coordinate action, but it may also conceal facts, so the actual conduct must be made clear as well. **Original scenario.** Broker prepares an account of the allocation that every party can accept; Opportunist says outright who received more. This may be a comic act of puncturing the story, or the start of questioning an unequal allocation. If there is no conduct requiring justification, a person's wording alone is not enough to classify them as Disregard. **Writing prompt:** “What do they know in private, and how much will each admit in public?” Research pathways: impression management and moral disengagement. [S12](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.46.3.598), [S13](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.71.2.364). These concern presentation and self-restraint respectively; our method does not combine them into ready-made measurement evidence for Justification / Disregard. ### M06 Exceptions and Mutual Shaping: This Time, Because It Is You, What Choice Did I Make? **Our perspective.** What makes a character relationship memorable is often an exception with a concrete cost: choosing to state the real options clearly, allowing the other person to refuse, or supporting a goal the other person has chosen for themselves. An exception must be established through action in a scene; it cannot be calculated automatically from two type codes. The two-way perspective matters especially here. A may already have changed a habitual response for B, while B reads it as ordinary cooperation. Both may be moving closer yet misreading how the other does so. Shared growth must identify who chose the goal of growth; “shaping you into what I prefer” cannot be written as the other person's self-actualization. **Original scenario.** Puppet Master usually arranges every route in advance, but with one particular person presents the options and consequences together and accepts that person's choice of another route. This may begin an intimate bond, but the story must still show whether the other person chooses to respond and whether that room for choice remains later. **Writing prompt:** “What would this person normally do? What changed this time? Did the other person recognize the change?” Research pathways: relationship specificity, unique attraction, support for the ideal self, and shared novel activities. [S14](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0065-2601(08)60144-6), [S15](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9280.2007.01897.x), [S16](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.77.2.293), [S17](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.78.2.273). Shared experiences can broaden the material of a relationship; they cannot replace trust, responsibility, or addressing specific harm. ## 4. Six Additional Kinds of Situational Information The four axes do not measure this information. Authors set it when writing fiction; analysis of real interaction requires observation or questions. If it is unknown, leave it unknown. | Situational question | Minimum detail to establish | Why it changes the relationship | |---|---|---| | Shared task | What are the two trying to accomplish or obtain together? | The same pair may stand on different sides in a joint task and in a contest for one place. | | Dependence and alternatives | Who controls information, resources, or permission, and who has other options? | Actual leverage may run counter to a character's preference for dominance. | | Current issue | Who wants the status quo to change, and who currently benefits from it? | The pursuer and withdrawer can switch places. | | Audience and rules | Who can see, and what account must hold up? | Private deals and public positions may constrain each other. | | History and investment | What was owed, honored, or misunderstood in the past? | History can make the same behavior read as goodwill or repeated harm. | | Autonomy and repair | Can either person refuse, pause, or leave; who will accept the consequences? | These choices determine how the story develops; type alone supplies no answer. | ## 5. Sixteen Same/Different Structures, Used Only to Find Questions Recording whether the two match or differ in the order “goal, method, stopping point, norm” produces 16 structures. “Same” means only the same side of an axis, not the same strength, ability, position, or life experience. “Different” does not mean their behavior will oppose each other every time. | Structure | Priority relationship question | |---|---| | Same–Same–Same–Same | With the same approach, who secures the position first, and can they recognize their shared blind spots? | | Different–Same–Same–Same | Their methods are similar, but can material gain and decision-making authority be satisfied separately? | | Same–Different–Same–Same | They want similar things but use different routes; can their actions connect? | | Same–Same–Different–Same | At what point is the matter over, and does one side still think the price was insufficient? | | Same–Same–Same–Different | Their actual goals and actions are similar, but do they have the same need for an outward explanation? | | Different–Different–Same–Same | Their aims and methods differ; how can they find a shared task? | | Different–Same–Different–Same | They can use similar methods, but do they disagree about the final prize and when to stop? | | Different–Same–Same–Different | With different goals and public accounts, will they undermine each other within the same plan? | | Same–Different–Different–Same | They want to reach the same place; how will they negotiate pace, route, and stopping conditions? | | Same–Different–Same–Different | Their methods and need for respectability differ; who bears the cost of acting openly and explaining it? | | Same–Same–Different–Different | They may proceed together at first; do they split over how to finish and explain it publicly? | | Different–Different–Different–Same | Can a shared acceptable account still conceal their differences in goals and action? | | Different–Different–Same–Different | Apart from a similar stopping point, what specific agreements do they need? | | Different–Same–Different–Different | Does familiarity with the other's methods become a language for negotiation or a basis for anticipating each other? | | Same–Different–Different–Different | Is their one similar goal enough to sustain the cooperation that follows? | | Different–Different–Different–Different | With differences on all four axes, what external task or personal choice can bring them into the same game? | For example, T01 × T09 differ only on the goal axis, so they are Different–Same–Same–Same. T13 × T16 match on goal and method but differ on stopping point and norm, so they are Same–Same–Different–Different. The number of matching axes may be used as a completeness check. It cannot be added up into a compatibility, danger, or “good ship” score. Nor must a pair differing on only one axis have an easier relationship than one differing on all four. ## 6. How to Write a Relationship Card 1. **Expand the characters.** Read both characters' four axes and role semantics; distinguish given tendencies from separately established abilities and experiences. 2. **Compare the four questions.** Record commonalities and differences and select the two most worth writing about. Check the remaining axes as well so the copy does not contradict the definitions. 3. **Place them in a situation.** Establish a task, a scarce resource, or an unresolved problem, and give the two different positions within it. 4. **Write each perspective.** How might A understand B, and B understand A? Use “may” to mark these as candidate interpretations and avoid claims of mind-reading. 5. **Select mechanisms.** Choose two or three. Their concrete operation should be visible in the structural rationale, three story branches, turning point, or ceasefire fields. 6. **Develop three branches.** Show how cooperation becomes possible, how conflict emerges, and how an intimate exception is created through voluntary action. Each branch needs its own conditions. 7. **Find a turning point.** Change one situational condition and observe how both respond anew. Then write one concrete ceasefire action instead of ending with “they communicate.” 8. **Condense it into a name.** Choose an image from an object, action, space, or contradiction recurring between them. Let the opening line explain in one sentence why it belongs to this pair. This sequence is a repeatable editorial check. The author must still give the task, leverage, and choices concrete form, then write them as observable interaction. ## 7. How Relationships Are Rewritten Over Time We organize stories around four moments: **entry, binding, fracture, rewriting**. These terms locate story beats; a story may skip, reverse, or repeat any of them. - **Entry:** Why do they approach each other—an opportunity, a shared task, a sense of similarity, or a need only the other can answer? - **Binding:** Why do they stay? What does each gain, and what does each pay? - **Fracture:** Which response is reinterpreted? Did the gains change, authority shift, an audience appear, or the original rules change unilaterally? - **Rewriting:** What action moves the relationship toward cooperation, conflict, intimacy, distance, or an ending? Do both accept the new arrangement? Take the “Leverage Pair” as an example: they enter through resource integration, bind through an exchange of gains and decision-making authority, and fracture when one side changes the allocation. Restating the terms and acknowledging the right to refuse may open another branch. Every arrow needs an action or condition as its bridge. ## 8. Naming for Recognition and Fan Creation Pairing 16 distinct types produces 120 combinations; adding 16 same-type combinations yields 136. Each pair keeps one primary name, shared by A × B and B × A, while the two perspectives remain separate. The name covers the character combination. Partnership, rivalry, and close bonds are optional narrative branches beneath it. Branches on one card may represent different timelines; readers may develop one without combining every fragment into a single canonical story. Names mainly use four approaches: a shared object, such as leverage or an outstanding balance; a continuing action, such as drawing the net closed; a shared space, such as adjacent seats or the same stage; or a central contradiction, such as a shared line punctured by one sentence. A name should sound natural, evoke the relationship, and accommodate multiple situations. All pairing names in this version are project-created candidates. They are not presented as psychological classifications or disguised as community names already in popular use. If user-created aliases are collected later, record the name, source, author's attribution preference, and date collected separately. Adopting one as the primary name is an explicit content-version update. The current primary checks for a name are: readers can identify the pair; one sentence can explain it; it differs from other names; and it still works when the storyline changes. A name cannot guarantee community uptake. Short chats with a few acquaintances serve only to find wording that is hard to read, misleading, or jarring. ## 9. A Note Website Readers Can See Directly > Every pair of characters has a name whose story can continue. Starting from what they contend for, how they move a situation, when they stop, and how they face rules, we organize their common ground, differences, and turning points. Partners, rivals, and close bonds are different directions their story may take; the specific relationship unfolds through the situation and both people's choices. To learn more, follow the mechanisms on a relationship card to read our analytical method and the related psychological research. A short note beside each relationship card is enough: “A reference for creating character relationships; it does not predict real-world pairing outcomes.” Put the fuller discussion of research scope on the method and sources page so every passage need not repeat the same long disclaimer. ## 10. How Editors Judge Whether the Content Is Good Enough **Structurally correct.** All 136 pairs are present, reciprocal lookup creates no duplicates, the 16 same-type pairs have clear situational positions, and axis meanings agree with the name mapping. **Concretely explained.** After reading, someone can say what the pair does together, where a disagreement is most likely to emerge in the story, and at least one way a situational change could alter it. If removing the names leaves text that could be assigned indiscriminately to dozens of pairs, it still needs revision. **Perspectives come in pairs.** A's goodwill cannot substitute for B's understanding, and A's desire for control cannot be treated as B's submission. A one-sided misreading can itself create a story, but the writing must identify whose misreading it is. **The turn is visible.** Show change through actions such as returning options, stating conditions, or stopping additional demands. Do not use “they suddenly understood” or “it was destined” as explanations. **Sources are represented honestly.** Research supports general mechanisms; the method and pairing content are identified as this project's proposals. Every research claim retains its original evidentiary status, and names do not serve as diagnoses or rankings of badness or relationship health. **Intimacy involves choice.** A story of intimacy may contain conflict and darkness, but respect for refusal, acceptance of consequences, and voluntary support are available forms of relationship change. Dramatic tension alone does not show that real-world harm is worth enduring. This round of source, content, and data checks is performed by Agent. If human feedback is used later, follow the project's established resource constraint: brief chats with no more than three or four acquaintances, focused on whether they understand the material and want to keep reading. Do not present this as statistical validation or psychometric validation.

Aron and colleagues used a newspaper questionnaire, a door-to-door survey, and three experiments to study couples’ shared participation in novel, arousing activities. In the surveys, shared “exciting” activities were associated with relationship satisfaction, and reduced boredom was one possible process. In the three experiments, couples who completed a novel, highly arousing seven-minute task together showed greater immediate improvement in relationship quality than couples who completed a mundane task. Comparisons with a no-activity condition also supported the conclusion that the change came from the novel task rather than merely from “doing something together.” [S17: Aron et al., 2000](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.78.2.273) **Where the evidence comes from:** The survey evidence is correlational; the experiments support short-term causal inferences. The outcomes measure immediate relationship experience before and after the activity. A seven-minute experiment is not a long-term intervention, and it cannot show that one exciting experience repairs problems accumulated over years. **Illustrative example:** Two people who constantly argue about procedures at the office sign up together for an unfamiliar two-person pottery class. Working through mistakes together lets each see the other’s judgment and reactions outside their old roles, briefly loosening the relationship. The example focuses on coordination in a shared new task; it does not treat danger or coerced participation as the source of attraction. **What this contributes to the project:** M06’s turning points can include a shared new task: a temporary alliance, switching roles for the first time, having to learn the other person’s method, or protecting a third person together. Kidnapping, threats, retaliation, or committing wrongdoing together cannot be used as proof of love. The experiments also do not guarantee that novel activities can repair an unsafe relationship.

## 它要回答什么\n\n坏人16型是一套关于“人会怎么坏”的类型系统：通过自测:
## What it asks

16 Shades is a system of types describing the forms harmful behavior can take. Through self-reflection or observation of others, it describes which shadow behavior style someone may lean toward in situations involving gain, competition, control, and conflict. It does not ask whether someone is a bad person.

## Four axes and 16 types

The four axes form a type in a fixed order: Goal (Gain / Control), Means (Strategy / Pressure), Harm (Instrumental / Punitive), and Norms (Justification / Disregard). Choosing one relatively preferred end on each axis produces 16 combinations. The first two axes define four families: Hunters, Raiders, Controllers, and Rulers.

## Five dimensions are separate from type

The four axes describe how someone acts. The five dimensions describe where harmfulness appears and to what degree: self-centeredness, orientation toward harm, instrumental manipulation, domination and retaliation, and resistance to normative restraint. Type is not a measure of how bad someone is, and style is not destiny.

## Limits of use

This is a custom framework for behavior styles and shadow patterns. It does not claim psychometric validation and is not intended for clinical diagnosis, legal classification, or a final judgment of anyone's overall worth.

## Project definition

The Goal axis describes relative priorities in relevant situations. **Gain** means benefits that can be owned, exchanged, or used. **Control** concerns who has the final say, who follows whom, and whether authority and standing are recognized. Ordinary protection of one's interests or fulfillment of management responsibilities is not treated as evidence of a shadow pattern.

## What to observe

Look beyond the apparent object. Control can serve gain, and gain can serve control. A more useful question is: when they conflict, which is the person willing to give up?

## Limits

This is an axis of action style, not a hierarchy of values. It does not establish the degree of harmfulness.

## Project definition

**Strategy** uses information, relationships, narratives, incentives, or the design of a situation to change the options someone sees and the choices they make. It can be open or conceal its intent. **Pressure** directly narrows another person's room to choose through orders, intimidation, conditions, resource advantages, or explicit consequences.

## What to observe

Legitimate negotiation, planning, and management skills are not in themselves evidence of harmfulness. Look at how the action treats the other person's information, choices, and boundaries.

## Limits

Strategy does not mean intelligence or introversion, and Pressure does not mean stupidity or impulsiveness. Either approach can be sophisticated or crude.

**Instrumental** harm serves an external goal. In principle, once that goal is reached, no additional harm is needed. **Punitive** harm treats making someone pay for refusal, offense, betrayal, or a challenge as valuable in itself. Further costs may follow even after the goal is achieved.

## What to observe

Distinguish unfinished repair from continued pursuit meant to cause discomfort after the issue is resolved. Punishment can be calm, sustained, and carried out through procedures.

## Limits

Instrumental does not mean less harm or greater compassion. Punitive does not mean uncontrolled rage. Legitimate accountability, limiting losses, and protecting boundaries do not automatically constitute harmfulness.

## Project definition

**Justification** values an appearance of reasonableness, legality, morality, procedure, or legitimate status, seeking a public defense for the behavior. **Disregard** relies less on approval from prevailing norms and may openly display boundary crossing, forcefulness, or indifference to judgment.

## What to observe

Ask how the action is presented, rather than relying on a single explanation. Who is the audience? What reputational risk does the public account address? Does the actual behavior bear its consequences?

## Limits

Justification does not mean genuinely following rules, and Disregard does not mean never using a narrative. Whether norms can actually stop or correct behavior belongs to the five-dimensional concept of resistance to normative restraint; this axis cannot stand in for it.

The first two axes define the families: Gain + Strategy forms the Hunters, Gain + Pressure the Raiders, Control + Strategy the Controllers, and Control + Pressure the Rulers. Actions and impacts can vary widely within one type, while different types can show similar degrees of harmfulness. Do not infer someone's worth, ability, or level of harm from a name or combination.

Type is not a measure of how bad someone is. A name cannot establish harm, a diagnosis, criminal status, or a relationship's outcome. Repeated behavior, specific circumstances, evidence, and alternative explanations matter more than labels.

先回答16道情境题，看看与你接近的人物。想了解更多，可以再答32题，或直接翻看人: Answer 16 questions to see which characters your choices resemble. For more detail, answer another 32 or browse the character profiles.
描述你在意什么、怎样行动，也说明哪些地方还不确定。: See what you prioritize and how you act, with room for what remains uncertain.
答题和完整解读无需注册。账号只用于保存和回看结果。: No account is needed for the test or the full interpretation. An account is only for saving and revisiting results.
不登录，也能看完整结果。账号只用于保存和回看结果。: No login needed for the full result. An account is just for saving and revisiting results.
你不必注册。答题、看完整解读，都可以直接开始。想把结果留到下次，再建个账号。: You don’t need an account. Take the test and read the full interpretation freely. Create an account when you want to save a result for later.
这里保留你最近保存的一份结果。: Your most recently saved result is kept here.
保存这张人物卡，或发给朋友看看。: Save this character card or send it to a friend.
遇到问题或有建议，欢迎告诉我们。复制反馈后，可以发到下面的联系邮箱。: Found a problem or have a suggestion? Copy your feedback and send it to the email below.
反馈已复制，可以发到联系邮箱。: Feedback copied. You can send it to our contact email.

在生活中可能怎样表现？: How might this show up in everyday life?
以下是根据回答推测的可能情况，不代表你已经遇到。你可以只读与你有关的部分。: The possibilities below are inferred from your answers; they do not mean you have experienced them. Read only the parts that feel relevant to you.
这一条只是初步线索。以下内容供你参考。: This is only an initial clue. The notes below are for reference.
如果你想换种做法: If you want to try a different approach
可以先不下结论: You can leave this open for now
可以先不下结论。: You can leave this open for now.
这份报告，只供你参考。: This report is here for your reference.
哪些地方贴近你的经验，哪些地方不贴近，都可以由你自己判断。: You can decide for yourself what fits your experience and what does not.
人物只是参照，你可以保留不同看法。: A character is only a reference. You may see it differently.
修复还没完成时，你可能会继续确认影响和责任，不急着翻篇。: When repair is unfinished, you may keep clarifying the impact and responsibility rather than move on quickly.
必要修复已完成后，若还要求对方认输或追加代价，关系可能反复卡在旧事里。: After necessary repair is complete, continued demands for surrender or extra costs can keep a relationship stuck in the past.
先分清：还缺什么修复，还是还想要更多代价。只处理前者。: First separate what still needs repair from the extra cost you may still want. Address the repair first.
补救明确后，你可能更愿意把分歧收住，看看关系接下来怎么走。: Once a remedy is clear, you may be more ready to bring the disagreement to a close and see where the relationship goes next.
若把事情处理好等同于感受也过去了，对方可能仍觉得没被听见。: If resolving the issue is treated as resolving the feeling too, the other person may still feel unheard.
事情处理了，你还有什么想说的？: The issue has been handled. Is there anything else you want to say?
这次两边都有线索：有的分歧能结束，有的仍需确认影响。: This time there are clues on both sides: some disagreements can end, while others still need their impact acknowledged.
不必急着把自己归为总会翻篇或总要追究；不同事情需要的修复不同。: There is no need to label yourself as someone who always moves on or always pursues it. Different situations need different repair.
如果想回看，可以问问当时还差什么。: If you want to look back, you might ask what was still missing then.
这条轴线索不足，报告不判断你在亲密关系中怎样收束分歧。: There are not enough clues on this axis for the report to say how you tend to close disagreements in close relationships.
信息不足时套用人物结论，容易把一次经历当成稳定模式。: Applying a character conclusion with too little information can turn one experience into a fixed pattern.
任务受阻时，你可能更愿意说清要求、期限和资源边界。: When work is blocked, you may be more ready to state requests, deadlines, and resource boundaries plainly.
若只强调后果而没有讨论空间，异议和风险可能拖到执行时才出现。: If consequences are emphasized without room to discuss, objections and risks may surface only during execution.
提出期限时，也留出能调整的条件。: When setting a deadline, leave room for conditions that can still be adjusted.
面对复杂协作时，你可能先整理信息、顺序和选项，让决定更好推进。: In complex collaboration, you may first organize information, sequence, and options to help a decision move forward.
若选项都朝预设结果排列，别人可能看不见其他可能，也难说出不同意见。: When every option points toward a preset result, others may not see other possibilities or find it easy to voice a different view.
给方案时，说清偏好，也留一个未列出的选项。: When offering a plan, state your preference and leave room for an option not yet listed.
这次两种路径都有线索，你可能会按任务和筹码选择不同做法。: This time both paths have clues. You may choose different approaches depending on the task and what is at stake.
不必用一次合作给自己定型；两种方式都可能帮忙，也都可能挤压选择。: There is no need to define yourself from one collaboration. Both approaches can help, and both can narrow choice.
如果想比较，可以看看对方实际有多少选择。: If you want to compare, consider how many real choices the other person had.
这条轴线索不足，报告不判断你在协作中更常怎么推进。: There are not enough clues on this axis for the report to say how you usually move collaboration forward.
缺少有效回答时套用协作风格，可能把角色设定当成你的实际做法。: Applying a collaboration style without enough valid answers can mistake character settings for your actual practice.
一起学习或分配资源时，你可能重视保留关键选择权，也愿意为方向一致多花些成本。: When learning together or allocating resources, you may value keeping key decision rights and accept some extra cost for shared direction.
若决定权比学习效果更重要，合适的资源或方法可能因不是由你主导而被放弃。: If decision rights matter more than learning outcomes, a useful resource or method may be dropped because you do not lead it.
共同选方法前，先说好什么证据能改变决定。: Before choosing a method together, agree on what evidence could change the decision.
一起学习或选资源时，你可能更愿意比较可用成果，也让合适的人负责决定。: When learning together or choosing resources, you may be more willing to compare usable outcomes and let the right person decide.
若只看眼前收益，基础、探索和长期积累可能因暂时没回报而被推迟。: If only immediate gains count, foundations, exploration, and long-term accumulation may be postponed because they do not pay off yet.
选资源时，也给长期目标留一点位置。: When choosing resources, leave some room for a long-term goal too.
这次两边都有线索，共同学习时的取舍可能随资源和责任变化。: This time there are clues on both sides. Trade-offs in shared learning may shift with resources and responsibility.
不必把一次资源选择当成固定学习特征；当时谁负责、方案差多大都很重要。: There is no need to treat one resource choice as a fixed learning trait. Who was responsible and how far the options differed both matter.
如果想回看，可以比较当时更看重成果还是主导。: If you want to look back, compare whether outcomes or control mattered more then.
这条轴线索不足，报告不推断你在共同学习或资源选择中的取向。: There are not enough clues on this axis for the report to infer your tendency in shared learning or resource choices.
遇到惯例不合适时，你可能更能按自己的判断作出选择，不必等所有人认同。: When a convention does not fit, you may be more able to choose by your own judgment without waiting for everyone to agree.
若共同意见只因不合个人判断就被排除，提醒边界和影响的反馈也可能失效。: If shared views are dismissed simply because they conflict with personal judgment, feedback about boundaries and impact may also be lost.
保留决定时，也听听自己可能漏掉的影响。: When keeping your decision, also listen for impacts you may have missed.
安排共同事务时，你可能愿意找大家能理解的依据，让规则和分工可讨论。: When arranging shared matters, you may look for reasons everyone can understand so rules and roles remain discussable.
若先定结果再找理由，真实分歧可能藏在表面道理后面。: If the result is decided first and reasons come later, the real disagreement may hide behind a plausible explanation.
说明共同理由时，也可以说清自己的偏好。: When explaining shared reasons, you can also state your own preference plainly.
这次两边都有线索，你在不同关系或规则里可能用不同依据作决定。: This time there are clues on both sides. You may use different grounds for decisions in different relationships or under different rules.
不必急着归为讲规则或只听自己；规则是否共享、决定影响谁都很重要。: There is no need to label yourself as rule-led or self-led. Whether rules are shared and whom a decision affects both matter.
如果想比较，可以看看决定实际影响了谁。: If you want to compare, consider whom the decision actually affected.
这条轴线索不足，报告不判断你在朋友与家庭中怎样为决定找依据。: There are not enough clues on this axis for the report to say how you find grounds for decisions with friends and family.
信息不足时贴上守规矩或不在乎评价的标签，都超出本次回答。: With too little information, labeling yourself as rule-following or unconcerned with others' views goes beyond these answers.
日常摩擦还没处理好时，你可能愿意继续确认遗漏的补救，不让表面恢复盖过问题。: When everyday friction is not resolved, you may keep checking for missed repair rather than let surface calm cover the issue.
若问题已补上，仍反复追求认输或代价，注意力可能难回到接下来的生活。: If the issue has been repaired but surrender or a price is still repeatedly pursued, attention may struggle to return to what comes next.
只分清一件还没完成的补救；没有的话，就到这里。: Name just one repair that remains unfinished. If there is none, it can end there.
日常摩擦处理后，你可能更容易停止投入，把时间和精力转回下一件事。: After everyday friction is handled, you may more easily stop investing in it and return your time and energy to the next thing.
若只确认事务结束，没说出的影响或必要复盘可能被跳过。: If only the task ending is confirmed, unspoken impact or useful review may be skipped.
恢复日程前，确认事情补上了吗，影响说明了吗。: Before returning to your routine, check whether the issue was repaired and the impact was explained.
这次两边都有线索，日常摩擦后的收束方式可能随补救和影响说明而变化。: This time there are clues on both sides. How everyday friction closes may vary with repair and whether the impact is addressed.
不必把这种差异泛化成稳定性格或心理状态；事件大小和关系都会改变它。: There is no need to generalize this difference into a stable trait or mental state. The event and relationship can both change it.
如果想回看，可以看看何时觉得事情已经结束。: If you want to look back, notice when the matter felt finished.
这条轴线索不足，报告不判断你在日常摩擦后怎样收束和恢复安排。: There are not enough clues on this axis for the report to say how you close everyday friction and return to routine.
线索不足时推断你容易放下或反复纠结，都可能把一次状态写成稳定模式。: Inferring that you easily let go or repeatedly dwell on things from too little evidence can turn one state into a stable pattern.
